subject: Questions regarding cut-points threshold (Roscoe et al. 2017)

messages.author: b2a542a12551e8c0
messages.subject: Questions regarding cut-points threshold (Roscoe et al. 2017)
parts:
Hello Dr Vincent,

I would like to ask for a clarification on the values for thresholds that we need to use for cut-points scaling.

This is my GGIR R script for part 5:
# Part 5:
             # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
             excludefirstlast.part5=TRUE,
             threshold.lig = c(5.3/85.7) * 1000, #threshold(s) for inactivity (can be more than one number)
             threshold.mod = c(8.6/85.7) * 1000, #threshold(s) for moderate activity (can be more than one number)
             threshold.vig = c(???/85.7) * 1000, #threshold(s) for vigorous activity (can be more than one number)

Thresholds for preschoolers given by Roscoe et al. 2017:

Sedentary <5.3 g/s
Light intensity 5.3-8.6 g/s
Moderate and above >8.6+

Is it possible to enter both threshold.mod and threshold.vig = c(8.6/85.7) *1000?
Or can we eliminate threshold.vig command as the threshold for vigorous intensity was not stated by the author?

Thank you for your help.

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Questions regarding cut-points threshold (Roscoe et al. 2017)
parts:
Hello Christine,

GGIR part 5 needs a theshold.vig. If no threshold is provide, it will use the default vallue, which may not be appropriate in this case.
To ignore vigorous give it a very high threshold, e.g. ten times as high as the moderate threshold you are using, In that way no vigorous activity will be detected.

Best regards,
Vincent
